festivals: Thiru Ulsavam / Arattu festival (10 days, Kumbham, February-March; grandest festival, held on Thiruvathira day)
Ezhara Ponnana Darshan (midnight of the 8th festival day; ceremonial procession and public display of the seven-and-a-half golden elephants)
Thulabharam (devotees weighed against offerings from gold to fruits)

history.dynasty: None (ancient temple; present structure reconstructed in 1542 CE; administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board)
history.period: Ancient (tradition); present temple reconstructed 1542 CE (717 ME)
history.summary: Ettumanoor Mahadeva Temple is one of the major ancient Shiva temples of Kerala and among its 108 Shiva temples, dedicated to Lord Shiva as Ettumanoorappan. Temple tradition holds that the Pandavas and the sage Vyasa worshipped here; the place name is traced to 'manoor' (the land of deer) or to 'Ettu Mana Ooru' (land of eight Namboothiri families / eight forms of Shiva). The present structure, with its gopuram, fortress walls, copper-plated roofs with 14 ornamental tops and a golden flagstaff topped with a bull, was reconstructed in 1542 CE (717 ME) and is famed for its Dravidian mural paintings, including the Pradosha Nritham (Dance of Shiva) fresco, among the finest in India. Adi Shankaracharya is believed to have composed the Soundarya Lahari while staying at this temple. The temple's great treasure is the Ezharaponnana - seven large and one small golden elephant, made of jackfruit wood and covered with nearly 13 kg of gold plates, donated by a Travancore king (tradition names Anizham Thirunal Marthanda Varma or his successor, with conflicting legends about the reason), kept in the vault and taken out once a year for public darshan.

name: Ettumanoor Mahadeva Temple
town_description: Ettumanoor is a town in Kottayam district of central Kerala, about 12 km north of Kottayam city on the Kochi-Kottayam route. It is famous above all for the Ettumanoor Mahadeva Temple, whose Ezharaponnana festival draws devotees from across Kerala and beyond. The town is also a well-known stopover for Sabarimala pilgrims travelling through the Kottayam region.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport (approx. 75-85 km; taxis and pre-paid cabs available).
travel.railway: Ettumanoor railway station (approx. 1-2 km); Kottayam Junction (approx. 12 km), well connected across Kerala and India.
travel.road: On the Ernakulam-Kottayam main road (approx. 12 km from Kottayam, 54 km from Ernakulam). Easily reached by KSRTC and private buses, autos and taxis.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. The annual 10-day Arattu festival in February-March (Kumbham), especially the 8th and 10th days with the Ezharaponnana darshan, is the most vibrant time but draws very heavy crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 4:00 AM to 12:00 noon; evening 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify — some sources list 4:00 AM-11:30 AM and 4:00 PM-7:30 PM; detailed pooja schedule varies by day). Traditionally entry to the sanctum is restricted to Hindus; photography is generally not allowed inside the temple premises. Men are expected to wear mundu (traditional attire) inside.
